answer: Lantern-tally identity pricing. Each new identity posts a publicly visible work receipt logged to a shared ledger, and the protocol raises the marginal price of the next identity whenever recent registrations rise. A mesa of idle identities above the current emission rate triggers a doubling of the receipt threshold for every subsequent slot. Attackers pay escalating compute and latency per sybil, while honest low-rate users face only a small marble-level fee. Duplicating identities thus costs more than the market value each fake agent can extract.
